purpose: Turn the R1 internal-control-plane blocker into an auditable contract split preflight before any physical move, public release claim, or release-switch change.

claim_boundary.allowed_user_claim: The internal-control-plane blocker now has a machine-checkable contract split preflight, consumer matrix, package-boundary snapshot, and future split gate.
forbidden_claims: The internal control plane has been physically moved.
R1 historical asset cleanup is complete.
The registry release action may proceed.

r1_blocker_execution_plan.selection_reason: Claude Code recommended first making the three-blocker execution plan explicit; Kimi recommended the largest pure engineering blocker first. This preflight combines both: it records the three-blocker plan, then performs the internal-control-plane preflight.

ordered_blockers.autonomous_scope: consumer matrix, package-boundary snapshot, future split gate, alias and rollback plan
ordered_blockers.human_boundary: Norven only needed if a later tranche proposes destructive cleanup, unrecoverable history loss, or public release risk acceptance.

ordered_blockers.autonomous_scope: future evidence retention and provider routing split can be prepared later without publishing.
ordered_blockers.human_boundary: Norven only needed for deleting or losing historical evidence.

ordered_blockers.autonomous_scope: compatibility inventory and tests can be prepared later.
ordered_blockers.human_boundary: Norven required before deciding whether Layer A compatibility is included in public RedCap product scope or retired.

roots.current_contract: Packaged for alpha readiness because root wrappers, revive/status/diagnose/closeout, release safety and validators still call these tools.
roots.future_target: internal/control-plane/tools with stable runtime facades and compatibility aliases

roots.current_contract: Packaged policy contracts used by runtime checks, release safety checks, file lookup, and human handoff documents.
roots.future_target: contracts/public for end-user/runtime contracts, contracts/internal for maintainer-only release/governance contracts

candidate_categories.meaning: Commands or policies required by revive/status/diagnose/doctor/closeout/help and clean workspace validation.
candidate_categories.release_posture: may remain package-visible if public help and contract wording are user-safe

candidate_categories.meaning: Validators, governance checks, release readiness checks and task-control helpers mainly used by maintainers.
candidate_categories.release_posture: must stay visibly labeled as maintainer/internal until a later physical split or public contract decision

candidate_categories.meaning: JSON or markdown contracts that tools read as truth sources.
candidate_categories.future_target: contracts/public or contracts/internal depending on consumer matrix
candidate_categories.release_posture: must not be moved without alias and consumer proof

consumer_matrix.split_risk: allowing package-safety or release-hard-gate checks to read stale policies
weakening closeout receipt and promise-ledger gates
breaking progressive disclosure and archaeology lookup
making independent review evidence unbindable to closeout

required_before_release_ready_claim: internal-control-plane no longer marked release-blocker-until-resolved, or formal release stays blocked
all package-visible control-plane paths have public/maintainer contract classification
no private archive, secret, local scratch, raw evidence, or host-local path appears in package candidates
future_split_gate.alias_strategy: Future physical moves must keep existing compass/** and references/** anchors resolvable through wrappers, import maps, or explicit alias resolver entries before path changes.
future_split_gate.rollback_strategy: Each future move tranche must be copy-first, verify, then delete-last; rollback must restore old anchors and package policy counts.

result.next_recommended_tranche: R1-prism-evidence-retention-split or a future internal-control-plane physical split, depending on formal release scope and package surface pressure.
